sentences.text:
This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellants/claimants challenging the award dated 13.08.2015 passed by the First Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (hereinafter referred to as "the Claims Tribunal"), District Datia (M.P.) in Claim Case No. 48/2013, whereby the claim petition filed by the appellants was dismissed.
2.

entities.text: First Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Brief facts of the case are that on 05.10.2011 at about 4:30 p.m., respondent No.1, Chandan Singh alias Chandu, while driving tractor bearing registration No. MP-32-M-5262 in a rash and negligent manner, hit the deceased Radhelal alias Radheshyam near the field of Murli.
The wheel of the tractor passed over the abdomen of the deceased, resulting in fracture of ribs.
Due to the injuries sustained in the said accident, Radhelal alias NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4809 2 MA-955-2015 Radheshyam succumbed to his injuries.
The claimants lodged a report against the driver of the offending vehicle at Police Station Sinawal, on the basis of which Crime No. 46/2015 was registered.
After due investigation, a charge-sheet was filed against the driver of the offending vehicle.
Thereafter, the appellants filed a claim petition seeking compensation.
The respondents filed their written statements and denied the averments made in the claim petition.
3. After framing the issues and recording evidence of both the parties, the Claims Tribunal dismissed the claim petition.

Kamal Kishor vs Chandu @ Chandan on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56385823/
1 4.
Being aggrieved by the impugned award, the appellants have preferred the present miscellaneous appeal contending that the award passed by the Claims Tribunal is contrary to settled principles of law.

It is submitted that the registration of FIR and filing of charge-sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle clearly establish the occurrence of the accident and the death of the deceased due to the said accident.
Despite this, the Claims Tribunal erred in rejecting the claim petition.

Hence, it is prayed that the impugned award be set aside.
5.
Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/Insurance Company opposed the appeal and prayed for its dismissal.
6. Learned counsel for the parties have been heard and the entire record of the Claims Tribunal has been perused.
7. The FIR (Ex.P.1) is reproduced as under :-

( )   
NEUTRAL CITATION
MPHC-GWL:4809 3 MA-955

"
8 . The FIR (Ex.P-1) reveals that the driver of the offending vehicle was driving the tractor in a rash and negligent manner, as a result of which the deceased died in the motor accident.
It is also evident that a charge-sheet was filed against the said driver.

9. From perusal of paragraph 14 of the impugned award, it appears that the Claims Tribunal held that the deceased was sitting on the mudguard of the tractor and that sitting on the mudguard is unsafe, and on that basis concluded that the deceased himself was responsible for the accident.

10. However, from the evidence of the claimants' witnesses as well as the FIR, it is clear that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, which resulted in the death of Radhelal alias Radheshyam.
11. This Court is of the considered opinion that the Claims Tribunal committed a manifest error in holding that the deceased himself was responsible for the accident.
Such a finding is not sustainable in the eyes of law and, therefore, the same deserves to be and is hereby set aside.

It is held that the deceased Radhelal alias Radheshyam died in the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving Kamal Kishor vs Chandu @ Chandan on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56385823/
2 of the driver of the offending vehicle.

12. From perusal of the impugned award, it is further apparent that the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:4809 4 MA-955-2015 Claims Tribunal did not assess the compensation payable to the claimants.
Therefore, the matter deserves to be remanded back to the Claims Tribunal for determination of the quantum of compensation and liability.
13. Consequently, the case is remanded to the Claims Tribunal for the limited purpose of assessing the amount of compensation payable to the claimants and fixing the liability.

The Tribunal shall afford due opportunity of hearing to both the parties on the issues of quantum of compensation and liability and thereafter decide the claim in accordance with law.
14.

Considering that the claim petition pertains to the year 2015, the Claims Tribunal is directed to decide the matter expeditiously, preferably within a period of six months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order.
15. The parties are directed to appear before the Claims Tribunal on 20/02/2026 and thereafter on such dates as may be fixed by the Tribunal.
16. There shall be no order as to costs.
Let a copy of this order along with the complete record be transmitted to the Claims Tribunal concerned for information and compliance.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE Prachi Kamal Kishor vs Chandu @ Chandan on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56385823/
